subject.title: Embedded session fence: false EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError on network filesystems (SMB/CIFS/Azure Files) — stat fingerprint mtimeNs/ctimeNs/ino flaps for unchanged files

question: Should embedded-session fencing accept a bounded content-equivalence check after metadata mismatch, or must deployments on network filesystems remain unsupported because inode/timestamp identity is part of the concurrency boundary?
rationale: The choice trades false completion failures on SMB/CIFS/NFS against the strength, cost, and semantics of the session-concurrency guard; repository source and existing tests need review before making that compatibility/security boundary change.

options.title: Add bounded content-equivalence fallback
options.body: After a metadata mismatch, accept only an unchanged bounded snapshot or digest and keep rejecting any content change.

options.title: Keep metadata-strict fencing
options.body: Preserve the current identity-and-time fence and document local-filesystem-only session storage for affected mounts.

options.title: Add an explicit compatibility mode
options.body: Keep strict behavior as default while offering a documented, tested content-based mode for network-mounted state.

recommendation.title: Add bounded content-equivalence fallback
recommendation.body: After a metadata mismatch, accept only an unchanged bounded snapshot or digest and keep rejecting any content change.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has the only concrete production and reproduction evidence available in this review context; code-history routing requires a successful repository inspection.
